speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue and unintentional weight loss; can you tell me how much weight you have lost and over what period of time? I also need to know if you have experienced any night sweats or fever recently.

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient reports a 6-month history of fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg (11 lb) despite maintaining a good appetite. He denies any recent changes in his diet or physical activity. He takes no medications and does not smoke or use illicit drugs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or swelling in your abdomen, particularly in the upper left side, or have you noticed any new lumps on your body? I also need to know if you have experienced any changes in your bowel habits or blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue. I also have 5 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, Good appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or shortness of breath? I also need to know if you have experienced any abdominal pain or fullness after eating small meals.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Patient denies any chronic illnesses or prior hospitalizations. Social history: Retired engineer; denies tobacco use or illicit drug use. Drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of diabetes, or have you noticed any recent increase in thirst or urination? I also need to know if you have experienced any abdominal pain, early satiety, or visible blood in your stool.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, changes in bowel or bladder habits, recent infections, or bleeding disorders.

text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 16,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 11 g/dL (low), Platelets Normal; Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the elevated white blood count and anemia, I need to check for signs of organ enlargement. Do you feel any fullness or pain in your upper left abdomen after eating small meals, which might suggest an enlarged spleen?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, changes in bowel or bladder habits, recent infections, or bleeding disorders.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Ultrasound: Nontender hepatosplenomegaly, Diffuse dullness over the left upper quadrant and right upper quadrant; Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Increased lymphocytes with smudge cells

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of smudge cells and lymphocytosis with hepatosplenomegaly strongly suggests Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia. REQUEST IMAGES
